t.1.63.1: Once that mighty-armed king, with abundant troops and mounts, went into a deep forest, surrounded by hundreds of horses and elephants.
t.1.63.2: He set out surrounded by hundreds of warriors, heroes bearing swords and spears, with maces and clubs in their hands, and holding lances and javelins.
t.1.63.3: With the lion-roars of the warriors, with the sounds of conches and kettledrums, and with the rumbling of chariot wheels, together with the trumpeting of the finest elephants,
t.1.63.4: As that king went forth, there arose a joyful shout of kilakilā, with cries of roaring and the slapping of arms, mingled with the sound of horses neighing.
t.1.63.7: This is that tiger among men, of wondrous prowess in battle; having encountered the might of his arms, the hosts of his enemies cease to exist.
t.1.63.8: Speaking such words, those women lovingly praised the lord of men, and they released showers of flowers upon his head.
t.1.63.6: The throngs of women there, watching him with weapon in hand, deemed him the equal of Śakra, a slayer of foes, one who could hold back the elephants of his enemies.
t.1.63.9: Praised on every side, here and there, by the foremost of brahmins, he set out with the greatest delight for the forest, eager to kill game.
t.1.63.10: Then the townsfolk and the country people followed him a very long way; afterwards, dismissed by the king, they turned back.
t.1.63.11: Then the lord of the earth, with his chariot resembling Suparṇa, filled the earth, and likewise filled the heavens with its roar.
t.1.63.12: As he went on, the wise one beheld a forest like Nandana, strewn with bilva, arka and khadira trees and crowded with kapittha and dhava trees.
t.1.63.14: Duḥṣanta, a tiger among men, together with his servants, troops and mounts, stirred up that forest, slaying beasts of many kinds.
t.1.63.13: It was rugged, covered with mountain ridges and rocks, waterless and empty of people, stretching for many yojanas, and filled with fearsome herds of wild beasts and other forest-dwelling creatures as well.
t.1.63.15: There Duḥṣanta struck down many packs of tigers that had come within range of his arrows, and pierced them through with his shafts.
t.1.63.16: That bull among men pierced some that stood far off with his arrows, and others that came near he cut down with his sword.
t.1.63.5: Standing on the rooftops of the finest palaces, the women there gazed upon that hero, radiant with supreme royal splendor, who had won glory for himself.
t.1.63.18: With javelins and with swords too, with maces, clubs and lances, he roamed there, striking down the wild beasts and birds of the forest.
t.1.63.17: Some antelopes he struck down with his spear, that best of the mighty; and, knowing the true art of whirling the mace in circles, he of boundless valor roamed about.
t.1.63.19: And as the great forest was churned up by the king of wondrous valor and by his warriors who delighted in battle, the great beasts abandoned it.
t.1.63.20: There the herds of deer, their groups scattered in flight and the leaders of their herds slain, then cried out here and there in their distress.
t.1.63.21: And coming upon a dried-up river, emaciated by despair of finding water, their hearts wearied by exertion, they fell down senseless.
t.1.63.23: Then some of the forest-dwellers produced fire and kindled it, and, having cut up the meat in the proper manner, they ate it.
t.1.63.24: There some powerful elephants in rut, wounded by weapons, curled up the tips of their trunks and, terrified, fled swiftly.
t.1.63.22: Overcome by hunger and thirst and worn out, some of the animals fell to the ground, and there they were devoured by the hungry tigers among men.
t.1.63.25: Voiding dung and urine and streaming much blood, the great wild elephants there trampled many men.
t.1.63.26: That forest, covered by the cloud of the army pouring down torrents of arrows, shone forth, strewn with buffaloes, its great beasts slain by the king.
